direct_answer: Outdoor steps and raised thresholds are common trip points. Handrails, good lighting, non-slip surfaces and small ramps can make getting in and out safer. Your council can assess your home, and minor adaptations are often free.

content:
Getting in and out of your home safely matters for independence.

This guide covers practical changes. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

Steps and paths

  • Handrails on one or both sides.
  • Outdoor lighting.
  • Non-slip surfaces.
  • Clear leaves and moss.

Door thresholds and small ramps

  • Raised thresholds are easy trip points, especially with a frame.
  • Small threshold ramps can smooth the step.
  • An occupational therapist can advise whether one is suitable.
  • Minor adaptations are often free after assessment.

Getting an assessment

Ask your council adult social care team. Larger works may qualify for a Disabled Facilities Grant.

In bad weather

  • Grit or salt steps.
  • Wear shoes with good grip.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Who fits handrails?

Often the council after assessment.

Do I need permission?

Tenants should ask their landlord.

Sources and further reading

  • NHS: Home adaptations
  • GOV.UK: Disabled Facilities Grants
  • NHS: Falls
